results.term_definition: A telescope is a device that collects photons (of visible light or other wavelengths) from distant objects and provides information (e.g. an image) about them to an observer. Early telescopes (from the beginning of the 17th century) used lenses as optical elements (see refracting telescope). Lenses are limited in how large they can be made, so in order to see fainter objects in greater detail with larger telescopes, mirrors (see reflecting telescope) were instead used to focus the light. The largest optical telescopes are reflecting telescopes. In the 20th century, telescopes for studying other regions of the electromagnetic spectrum were invented, so there now exist radio telescopes, infrared telescopes, X-ray telescopes, etc. Because celestial sources are faint, astronomers tend to build large aperture telescopes to collect more light and reach finer angular resolutions.
